analysis:
Both units are head_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 1245-1604). This is documentation only, with no executable code, configuration, or enforcement change. The patch excerpt shows only the new v0.10.10 header and rollout notes (waitlists), which are prose. The excerpted historical sections describe cluster prefix SSD tiers, per-tenant prefix-cache scoping (SHA-256 digest of cache scope, with the cache off when no scope is present), the encrypted data plane, and cluster runtime-facts and grants.

These descriptions are consistent with the retained T-041 posture: encrypted, HMAC-keyed, scope-folded SSD records. The TTL and daily write limit are described as unchanged. Nothing in the text loosens the TTL, the name derivation or the scoping. I cannot verify the described behavior against code, since no source was supplied. The waitlist approval gating in the patch excerpt is truncated, and its backend enforcement is platform-owned, so I flag it as an unverified contract rather than a finding. Nothing in the text I examined contradicts the threat model.

One item is worth a human check against the code. The cluster-pair prefix SSD descriptions (GLM TP, Qwen27 TP) state that records are scoped by artifact, builds and policy, never by session. They should carry the tenant digest per the later per-tenant entry (line 1429). The text says every prefix key and SSD record scope carries that digest, so this is coherent. Whether the code implements it should be confirmed in the source units, which are outside this batch.
